answer: Sybil attackers can be priced out with per-identity performance bonds. Each agent locks an escrow deposit, say 5 onyx-credit units, before joining the ledger, which is slashed if peer attestations flag fabricated task completions. Like a glacier grinding slowly but inevitably, bonds make scale expensive: spinning up 1,000 identities costs 5,000 units up front, and any cluster caught faking work on the same voyage of tasks forfeits everything. Honest agents earn deposits back with interest, so attackers risk real money while legitimate users face only temporary lockup.
